rationale: This is a linear rank-sum of two separately published anomalies (book-to-market and Boudoukh–Michaely–Richardson–Roberts net payout yield) with no genuine interaction — the "intersection" story is not what SUMRANK computes, since a firm extreme on one leg alone lands in the tails.

Adding net repurchases to earnings in the numerator of a market-cap-scaled yield is arithmetically just E/P plus net-payout-yield, i.e. a known-anomaly sum rather than a cross-theme interaction, and the un-COALESCEd prstkc/sstk will silently drop firms that report neither (economically zero-flow firms), biasing coverage inconsistently with the sibling proposals.

The conditional construction is thoughtfully sign-aligned, but (i) the hypothesis says off-diagonal cells carry "no signal" while the expression actually assigns cheap-issuers a negative and rich-repurchasers a positive score, and (ii) buyback drift concentrated in high book-to-market firms is a long-published result (Ikenberry–Lakonishok–Vermaelen; Peyer–Vermaelen), so this is close to a rediscovery; the /at inside both INDICATORs is also redundant since only the sign matters.

Economically the most coherent pairing here (enterprise multiple with total net external financing), but both components are published anomalies (Loughran–Wellman; Bradshaw–Richardson–Sloan) and SUMRANK imposes no interaction whatsoever, so the test cannot distinguish the joint mechanism from the additive average of two known effects, while dltis/dltr sparsity will erode coverage.

The persistence-of-financing-state dimension is a genuinely non-obvious refinement over one-shot issuance measures and the multiplicative form does concentrate the long leg in the cheap-and-committed corner, but the short leg degenerates into a large mass of exact zeros (all non-repurchasers plus all expensive firms), which risks unstable portfolio composition, and the 5-year TS_SUM plus un-COALESCEd prstkc/sstk will cut coverage materially.

The expression's natural direction contradicts the stated story: because the P/B rank multiplies a signed issuance average, the extreme long leg is populated by high-multiple *repurchasers* (large negative product), not by value firms, so the tested spread is glamour-buyback versus glamour-dilution rather than the intended valuation-conditioned dilution effect — and the underlying net-issuance anomaly is already well documented (Pontiff–Woodgate, Daniel–Titman).
